text: Add the complete impression-time request-context feature group to the neutral additive user/video scaffold: tab, hour, and weekday encoded with train-only vocabularies and explicit unknown handling.
rationale: This is the highest-priority measured feature change: the training-only temporal screen found positive primary lift on every holdout day and full coverage. It can alter within-user ordering because context varies across impressions.
exact_ablation: Add only the request_context group consisting of tab, hour, and weekday; leave the additive architecture, BCE training, IDs, optimizer, and all other inputs unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.003 relative to the seed implementation; the measured screen lift was +0.00221 in primary.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small increase or near-flat result, approximately -0.001 to +0.002; the screen supports ranking value but does not establish a top-five-specific gain.

text: Add only the tab request-context field to the neutral additive user/video scaffold, using a train-fitted categorical encoding.
rationale: Tab is an isolated, low-cost test of whether the positive request-context screen is driven by coarse placement or surface context rather than time. It preserves a clean interpretation and avoids broad feature expansion.
exact_ablation: Add only tab as a categorical feature; exclude hour, weekday, and every other non-ID feature, with architecture and training unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely modest increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.002, but below the full request-context group if temporal information is important.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely near-flat to slightly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.0015; coarse context may not reliably fix the top five.

text: Add only impression hour and weekday, represented as cyclic time features, to the neutral additive user/video scaffold.
rationale: This isolates the temporal portion of the only positively screened feature family. Cyclic encoding can represent adjacent-hour similarity without adding high-cardinality interactions.
exact_ablation: Add only impression-time hour and weekday using cyclic transforms; omit tab and all other non-ID features, while retaining the seed architecture and training procedure.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely positive, approximately +0.0008 to +0.0025, if user preferences vary by time of day.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely small positive or neutral, approximately -0.0005 to +0.0015; temporal effects may improve broad ordering more than top-five precision.

text: Replace the additive ID scorer with a latent user-video interaction scorer using train-fitted user and video embeddings and a dot-product interaction, without adding metadata or context.
rationale: The seed's additive user and video effects cannot express personalized user-video affinity. A dot-product interaction is a single architecture ablation that directly creates candidate-specific variation within a user.
exact_ablation: Replace the additive user-plus-video logit with global bias plus user/video embeddings and their dot product; retain only user_id and video_id inputs and the same pointwise training setup.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential increase on warm user-video traffic, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, with no expected benefit for unseen entities.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential increase on warm traffic, approximately 0 to +0.003, but it may fall if sparse interactions overfit and disrupt top-ranked items.

text: Replace the additive ID scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer over user_id and video_id only, retaining the same labels and pointwise BCE objective.
rationale: A nonlinear scorer can model interactions beyond additive effects while keeping the feature contract minimal. The change is materially different from a dot-product factorization and has a direct implementation path.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive linear scoring architecture with 32-dimensional user/video embeddings followed by a two-layer MLP; keep inputs, loss, optimizer, and split unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Possible increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, if nonlinear identity interactions generalize beyond memorized biases.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Possible small increase, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; extra capacity may improve or destabilize the top five.

text: Add a two-layer low-rank cross branch to an embedding-plus-MLP scorer using only user_id and video_id embeddings, while retaining the existing deep branch.
rationale: Explicit bounded-order crosses offer a distinct mechanism from a plain MLP and may improve personalized interactions. The measured ID screen establishes that identity inputs are relevant enough to justify an interaction-focused architecture test.
exact_ablation: Add only a two-layer low-rank cross branch to the user/video embedding-plus-MLP architecture; keep the feature set, pointwise BCE loss, and optimization schedule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential modest increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.003, concentrated on warm entities.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential increase of 0 to +0.0025, with a meaningful risk of no gain if sparse crosses memorize training identities.

text: Replace ordinary impression-weighted BCE with exact inverse-candidate-count, user-normalized BCE on the neutral additive user/video scaffold.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ranking, while ordinary minibatch BCE can be dominated by users or groups with many impressions. User-normalized BCE is a clean loss-only ablation that may align optimization with the evaluation population.
exact_ablation: Change only the reduction from ordinary BCE to complete-group inverse candidate-count weighting of 1 divided by group size; retain architecture, features, optimizer, and schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely modest increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, especially if candidate-count imbalance is substantial.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to slightly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, because the loss remains pointwise and does not directly target rank five.

text: Add an nDCG@5-weighted pairwise logistic term to the neutral additive user/video scorer while retaining ordinary BCE as the base loss.
rationale: The measured request-context screen shows that broad ranking signal exists but does not establish top-five gains. A LambdaRank-style term directly targets positive-negative swaps affecting the first five positions, making this a distinct objective ablation.
exact_ablation: Add only a normalized LambdaRank-style nDCG@5 swap-weighted pairwise term with fixed coefficient 0.1 to ordinary BCE; keep the seed feature set and architecture unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Could increase slightly or remain flat, approximately -0.001 to +0.002, because top-five emphasis may sacrifice broad pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Most plausible gain, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, provided training groups faithfully match displayed candidate groups.

text: Change the training sampler from shuffled natural-order minibatches to user-balanced minibatches, with each selected user contributing an equal number of training impressions, while leaving the model and loss unchanged.
rationale: This tests whether optimization is distorted by prolific users without changing the scoring function. It is conceptually distinct from user-normalized BCE because the ablation changes example presentation and sampling rather than the loss formula.
exact_ablation: Replace only the natural shuffled minibatch sampler with user-balanced sampling that gives each sampled training user equal batch mass; retain all features, architecture, BCE, and evaluation data.

expected_effect.GAUC: Possible modest increase, approximately 0 to +0.0025, if user imbalance currently dominates updates.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to slightly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.0015; sampling may increase variance and harm rare-item ordering.

text: Add train-only time-of-day interaction features between user identity and request context through a fixed user-by-tab cross feature, without adding any other context fields.
rationale: The request-context screen is positive overall and stable by day, but the additive seed cannot express that a user's response to a tab varies by context. A single hashed user-tab cross is a targeted feature ablation rather than a broad feature expansion.
exact_ablation: Add only one train-fitted user_id-by-tab cross feature with an explicit unknown bucket; retain the seed's separate user and video IDs, architecture, loss, and optimizer.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential increase of approximately +0.0005 to +0.003 if context-specific personalization exists; sparse users may see no benefit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential increase of approximately 0 to +0.002, with risk of top-five degradation from rare-cross overfitting.

text: Replace the zero-initialized additive weights with small deterministic random initialization, keeping the neutral additive architecture, IDs, BCE loss, and optimizer unchanged.
rationale: The seed initializes every feature weight to zero, which can create a symmetric starting point. A controlled initialization ablation is cheap and tests whether early optimization dynamics affect ranking without changing the model's representational capacity.
exact_ablation: Change only weight initialization from all zeros to deterministic zero-mean Gaussian values with standard deviation 0.01; retain every feature, architecture equation, loss, and training hyperparameter.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely flat to slightly positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.0015; the representational model is unchanged.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely flat, approximately -0.001 to +0.001; any movement may be seed-sensitive rather than systematic.

text: Add only the request-context group to a user-normalized BCE training objective while retaining the neutral additive scorer and no other feature families.
rationale: This combines the strongest measured feature family with a single defined objective configuration, testing whether its positive screen lift survives user-level loss normalization. It is a concrete alternative to the feature-only confirmation and may better align updates with within-user evaluation.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed configuration with exactly one joint configuration change: add request_context and use user-normalized BCE as its training objective; do not alter architecture, sampler, or any other feature family.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely positive, approximately +0.001 to +0.0035, with possible improvement over feature-only training if group imbalance is harmful.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.0025; the pointwise normalized loss still does not explicitly optimize top-five swaps.
